specification.problem: Approximate a single-qubit unitary U within precision epsilon by a Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) circuit over Clifford+T with one ancilla and measurement. Scoped instance: one RUS attempt, a measurement-free 2-qubit Clifford+T unitary W whose ancilla-|0> success branch implements a non-unitary Kraus operator proportional to a unitary V approximating U = R_z(theta).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only a tiny, assumed single-attempt unitary W on system q0 and ancilla q1 is specified, together with the Kraus-operator, success-probability and expected-T-count relations. The randomized polynomial-time classical synthesis (sampling Z[1/sqrt2,i] entries, norm-equation solving with randomized factoring), the paper's actual circuit family, the failure-branch correction, the retry loop and numerical T-count comparisons are outside scope. The concrete W is a placeholder illustration, not the paper's construction.

symbols.meaning: Clifford+T unitary of one RUS attempt on system and ancilla
Kraus operators for ancilla outcome 0 (success) and 1 (failure)
scalar with |c|^2 = success probability p (state-independent when K_0 = cV)

equations.label: Kraus operators of one attempt
equations.description: Ancilla prepared in |0>, W applied, ancilla measured in the computational basis; completeness follows from unitarity of W.
equations.justification: Standard Kraus-operator formalism for ancilla-assisted measurement.

equations.label: Success operator proportional to a unitary
equations.description: Success branch acts as a unitary V close to U with success probability p, so K_0^dagger K_0 = p I.
equations.abstract_quote: approximate any given single-qubit unitary within precision $\varepsilon$
equations.justification: Approximating U by an RUS circuit requires the success branch to be a unitary approximating U; proportionality to a unitary is the assumed structure from the method sketch.
assumptions: Norm is the operator norm, up to global phase

equations.label: Expected T-count
equations.description: Expected T-count of the repeat-until-success loop with geometric number of attempts, ignoring failure-correction T cost.
equations.justification: Geometric retry statistics give expected attempts 1/p; correction gates are assumed free of T.
assumptions: Failure correction costs no T gates

equations.label: Ancilla-free reference bound
equations.description: Reference lower bound and the reported average ratio of about 2.5.
equations.abstract_quote: theoretical lower bound of $3\log_{2}(1/\varepsilon)$ for ancilla-free single-qubit circuit decomposition
equations.justification: The abstract states the bound and the 2.5 average factor (numerical evidence, not derived here).
assumptions: Ratio is an empirical average, not a guarantee per instance

equations.label: Target rotation
equations.justification: The scope is chosen as one small instance since the abstract gives no explicit U.
assumptions: theta fixed classically, e.g. pi/8-type angle

registers.name: q0
registers.role: system qubit, arbitrary input state; qubit 0

registers.name: q1
registers.role: ancilla, initialized |0>, success when measured 0; qubit 1

steps.description: Prepare ancilla in |0> and system in the input state; basis ordering |q1 q0>, little-endian as in Qiskit.

Apply a fixed Clifford+T attempt unitary W on (q0,q1), e.g. H on ancilla, controlled Clifford+T blocks with T and T-dagger, closing H on ancilla. The specific W must be supplied by classical search; no paper-specific W is known.
Success branch is ancilla outcome 0, giving K_0=cV with V close to U; the measurement and retry loop are outside the unitary circuit.
Classically, compute expected T-count T_a/p and compare to the ancilla-free reference.

specification.measurement: Ancilla q1 measured in the computational basis after W; outcome 0 is success. Not included in the built unitary.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Retry on failure after a fixed correction; the randomized polynomial-time search over Z[1/sqrt2,i] candidates with norm-equation solving and the filtering ||V-U||<=epsilon is described qualitatively only.
assumptions: Scope is a single attempt for U=R_z(theta) with fixed theta
W is a placeholder Clifford+T circuit whose exact gates are not given by the abstract
Failure branch is correctable by Cliffords at no T cost
missing_information: Explicit gate sequence W of the paper's RUS circuits
